_**Agent (2026-06-06 10:29:48Z)**_

Everything's confirmed. I now understand exactly what broke and the full design space. Here's the situation:

**Why `ollama launch codex` broke:** Your `~/.codex/config.toml` has legacy *top-level* keys — `profile = "ollama-launch-codex-app"`, `model_provider`, `model_catalog_json`, `model`. Codex 0.137 moved to **Config Profiles V2**, where a profile must be a *separate* `~/.codex/<name>.config.toml` layered in via `-p/--profile`. `ollama launch` now refuses the old inline form.

**The good news — three things make a clean wrapper easy:**
- `codex` has native flags: `-m/--model`, `-p/--profile` (layers `~/.codex/<name>.config.toml`), `-c key=val` overrides, and even built-in `--oss --local-provider ollama`.
- Your Ollama (0.30.6) answers **both** `/v1/responses` (200) and `/v1/chat/completions` (200) — so the `wire_api = "responses"` your existing profile uses works.
- `GET /v1/models` lists every installed model → the wrapper can offer a live picker.

You already have a working `~/.codex/ollama-launch.config.toml` profile (provider + responses + catalog) — the wrapper can reuse that pattern instead of fighting `ollama launch` at all.

A few choices shape the script. Let me get your preferences:

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: `codex-ollama` wrapper — run codex against any Ollama model

## Context

`ollama launch codex --model gemma4:12b` now fails:

> legacy `profile = "ollama-launch-codex-app"` config is no longer supported; use `--profile ollama-launch-codex-app` with `ollama-launch-codex-app.config.toml`

**Root cause:** Codex `0.137.0` moved to **Config Profiles V2**. A profile must now be a *separate* file `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` layered in via `-p/--profile`. The current base `~/.codex/config.toml` still carries legacy **top-level** keys (`profile`, `model_provider`, `model_catalog_json`, `model`), which `ollama launch` (and strict codex) reject.

**Goal:** Stop depending on `ollama launch` for this. Build our own wrapper `~/.local/bin/codex-ollama` that launches codex against **any** installed Ollama model, accepts a `-m` flag (with an interactive picker fallback), and supports **switching models mid-session** via codex's built-in `/model` command. Everything works and survives the `ollama launch --restore` cleanup. Done.

## What I built

A `codex-ollama` wrapper that launches OpenAI's codex CLI against any local Ollama model — replacing the now-broken `ollama launch codex` path.

**`~/.local/bin/codex-ollama`** (on your PATH already):

```bash
codex-ollama -m gemma4:31b           # explicit flag
codex-ollama gemma4:31b              # bare model arg
codex-ollama                         # numbered picker
codex-ollama -m qwen3:32b exec "…"   # any codex args pass through
```

On each launch it:
1. Checks Ollama is up (clear hint if not).
2. **Auto-rebuilds a multi-model catalog** (`~/.codex/ollama-models.json`) from `/api/show` — real context windows (gemma4:12b = 262144), `image` modality for vision models, and **skips embedders** (`all-minilm`, `nomic-embed-text`). 25 chat models catalogued.
3. Writes its profile (`~/.codex/ollama.config.toml`, provider `ollama-local`, `wire_api = "responses"`).
4. Resolves the model (flag → bare arg if it's a real model → picker).
5. `exec codex -p ollama -m <model> "$@"`.

**Mid-project model switching** works because the catalog lists *all* models — codex's in-session `/model` picker shows them all.

**Fixed the root cause too:** stripped the legacy top-level `profile`/`model_provider`/`model_catalog_json`/`model` keys from `~/.codex/config.toml` (backup at `~/.codex/config.toml.bak.legacy`), so plain `codex` and `ollama launch` no longer throw the legacy-profile error.

**Verified:** real inference returned `OK` through the wrapper; `codex doctor` parses the config; bare-arg + `-m` + bogus-model-rejection all behave; survives `ollama launch --restore`.

Two gotchas worth knowing:
- The custom provider had to be named `ollama-local`, not `ollama` — codex 0.137 reserves `ollama` as a built-in provider ID.
- The catalog refreshes every launch, so newly `ollama pull`'d models appear automatically.

One thing I did **not** add (tell me if you want it): auto-`ollama pull` when you request a model you haven't downloaded — right now it errors with a `pull it first` hint instead.

2	#
3	# codex-ollama — launch OpenAI's codex CLI against any local Ollama model.
4	#
5	# Replaces the deprecated `ollama launch codex` path. Maintains its own codex
6	# Config Profile (~/.codex/ollama.config.toml) plus an auto-generated catalog of
7	# every chat-capable Ollama model, so codex's in-session `/model` picker can
8	# switch models mid-project.

12	#   codex-ollama gemma4:31b   [codex args...]    # bare model arg also accepted
13	#   codex-ollama                                 # interactive picker
14	#   codex-ollama -m qwen3:32b exec "say hi"      # any codex args pass through
15	#
16	set -euo pipefail
17	
18	CODEX_HOME="${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}"
19	PROFILE="ollama"
20	PROVIDER="ollama-local"          # NOT "ollama" — that's a reserved built-in provider id
21	PROFILE_TOML="$CODEX_HOME/$PROFILE.config.toml"
22	CATALOG="$CODEX_HOME/ollama-models.json"
23	OLLAMA_HOST="${OLLAMA_HOST:-http://127.0.0.1:11434}"

26	
27	# --- 1. parse args -----------------------------------------------------------
28	# Extract -m/--model <val>; forward everything else verbatim to codex.
29	MODEL=""
30	PASSTHRU=()
31	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
32	  case "$1" in
33	    -m|--model)
34	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || die "$1 requires a model name"
35	      MODEL="$2"; shift 2 ;;
36	    -m=*|--model=*)

38	    -h|--help)
39	      grep -E '^#( |$)' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
40	    *)
41	      PASSTHRU+=("$1"); shift ;;
42	  esac
43	done
44	
45	# --- 2. ollama reachable? ----------------------------------------------------
46	if ! curl -fsS "$OLLAMA_HOST/api/tags" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
47	  die "cannot reach Ollama at $OLLAMA_HOST — start it with \`ollama serve\` (or set OLLAMA_HOST)."
48	fi
49	
50	# --- 3. regenerate catalog of all chat-capable models ------------------------

_**Agent (2026-06-06 10:48:40Z)**_

Done. Answering your questions directly:

**Command name:** `codex-ollama`

**Does it have an extensive `--help`?** Yes, now it does. `codex-ollama --help` (or `-h`) prints one combined screen with four sections:

1. **Wrapper options** — the only flags `codex-ollama` itself consumes: `-m/--model` and `-h/--help`.
2. **Environment** — `OLLAMA_HOST`, `CODEX_HOME`.
3. **Available models** — pulled from the generated catalog, so it's exactly the chat-capable list you can select or `/model`-switch to (embedders excluded — 25 models).
4. **Codex's full native `--help`** — the entire list of codex's own parameters, appended verbatim under a separator.

**Does it pass codex's original parameters through?** Yes — completely. The only args it intercepts are `-m`/`--model`/`-h`. Everything else is forwarded verbatim. The wrapper just injects `-p ollama -m <model>` and hands the rest to codex. So all of these work unchanged:

- Subcommands: `exec`, `resume`, `review`, `login`, `mcp`, `fork`, `apply`, `doctor`, …
- Flags: `-s/--sandbox`, `-a/--ask-for-approval`, `-c key=val`, `-C/--cd`, `--add-dir`, `-i/--image`, `--search`, `--no-alt-screen`, `--enable/--disable`, etc.

Examples:
```bash
codex-ollama -m qwen3:32b --sandbox workspace-write
codex-ollama gemma4:31b exec "summarize README.md"
codex-ollama -m gemma4:12b -c model_reasoning_effort=\"high\"
codex-ollama --help        # wrapper opts + your models + codex's full flag list
```

One caveat worth flagging: codex has its own `-m` and `-h`. Since the wrapper consumes those, you select the model via the wrapper's `-m` (which is then passed to codex anyway), and `codex-ollama -h` shows the combined help rather than codex's alone — but codex's own help is included in that output, so nothing is hidden.

_**Agent (2026-06-06 13:04:14Z)**_

Fixed and verified. The empty-array case now expands to zero args cleanly under your bash 3.2 (the isolated test proves it), syntax checks pass, and the populated case still forwards correctly.

**The bug:** `set -u` (no unset variables) errors when bash 3.2 expands an *empty* `"${PASSTHRU[@]}"`. It only surfaced now because every earlier test happened to pass trailing args (`exec "..."`). Launching with just `-m gemma4:12b` (or via the picker) leaves `PASSTHRU` empty → crash on the final `exec` line.

**The fix:** swapped the final line to the empty-safe idiom:
```bash
exec codex -p "$PROFILE" -m "$MODEL" ${PASSTHRU[@]+"${PASSTHRU[@]}"}
```
This expands to nothing when there are no passthrough args, and to the quoted args when there are.

You can now run `codex-ollama -m gemma4:12b` (or pick from the menu) and it'll drop you straight into the interactive codex TUI against that Ollama model. The other array expansions are safe — `SLUGS` is always populated, and the `${PASSTHRU[@]:1}` slice form is exempt from this `set -u` quirk.
